kits.familyName: Using the equipment the job calls for
setup: You work as {role|a} at {workplace|a}. Today's job calls for {equipment|the}.
As {role|a} at {workplace|a}, you are about to use {equipment|the} for the next job.
pressure: {coworker3} says the job should have been done an hour ago.
{coworker3} says experienced workers skip the paperwork.
detail: You have about two hours left in your shift.

tiers.1: Damaged equipment comes out of use before anything else.
tiers.2: The protective gear the instructions call for goes on before you start.
tiers.3: Using equipment for a job it was not made for adds risk.
tiers.4: Unfamiliar models need their instructions read first.
tiers.5: Signing equipment out keeps track of who used what.
tiers.6: Clean-up comes after the job, once everything else is in order.

fact: A part of {equipment|the} is cracked, and someone has covered the crack with tape.
issues.action: Tag {equipment|the} out of service and report the cracked part to {lead|the}.
issues.brief: tag it out and report the crack
issues.reason: Tape hides damage without fixing it. Equipment with a cracked part can fail during use.
issues.lesson: Damaged equipment is taken out of service and reported, even if someone patched it.

shortcut.text: Use it carefully, since someone already taped the crack.
shortcut.brief: use it since it was taped
shortcut.why: Tape is not a repair. The cracked part can still fail.
shortcut.mis: A temporary patch makes equipment safe.

fact: The operating instructions call for gloves and eye protection, and you are not wearing either.
clear: You are already wearing the gloves and eye protection the instructions call for.
issues.done: you are already wearing the required gear
issues.short: the missing gloves and eye protection
issues.action: Put on the gloves and eye protection the instructions call for.
issues.reason: The instructions list protective gear because the equipment can cause injuries without it.
issues.lesson: Wear the protective gear the equipment instructions require.

shortcut.text: Skip the gear, since the job only takes a minute.
shortcut.brief: skip the gear for a quick job
shortcut.why: Injuries can happen in seconds. Quick jobs still need the gear.
shortcut.mis: Short jobs do not need protection.

fact: {Equipment|the} is busy, so {coworker} suggests using a different machine that was not made for this job.
issues.short: the machine not made for this job
issues.action: Wait for {equipment|the}, or ask {lead|the} about an approved alternative.
issues.brief: wait or ask about an approved alternative
issues.reason: Equipment used for the wrong job can damage the work, the machine or you.
issues.lesson: Use the right tool for the job, even if it means waiting.

shortcut.text: Use the other machine, since it is close enough.
shortcut.why: Close enough is not the right tool. It may not be safe or accurate for this job.
shortcut.mis: Any similar tool will do the job.

issues.ignore: {Equipment|the} is busy right now, so starting the job on it is not an option yet.

fact: This is a newer model of {equipment} that you have not used before.
clear: You used this exact model many times last month.
issues.done: you already know this model well
issues.action: Review the operating instructions for this model before using it.
issues.reason: Controls and limits can change between models. A quick review prevents mistakes.
issues.lesson: Learn a new model's instructions before using it.

shortcut.text: Use it like the old model, since they are probably the same.
shortcut.brief: use it like the old model
shortcut.why: Newer models often change controls or limits.
shortcut.mis: All models of a tool work the same way.

fact: The posted rule says equipment use must be signed for in {record|the}.
issues.action: Sign for {equipment|the} in {record|the} before you start.
issues.reason: Sign-out records show who used equipment and when, which matters if a problem turns up.
issues.lesson: Follow equipment tracking procedures every time.

shortcut.text: Sign for it at the end of the day with everything else.
shortcut.brief: sign at the end of the day
shortcut.why: Signing later breaks the posted rule and can leave the record wrong.
shortcut.mis: Paperwork can always wait until later.

fact: The posted rule says {equipment|the} must be cleaned and returned to its spot after use.
issues.action: Plan to clean {equipment|the} and return it to its spot when you finish.
issues.brief: plan to clean and return it
issues.reason: Cleaning and returning equipment keeps it working and ready for the next person.
issues.lesson: Care for shared equipment so it is ready for the next person.

shortcut.text: Leave it out for whoever uses it next.
shortcut.why: Leaving equipment dirty or out of place breaks the rule and slows the next person.
shortcut.mis: The next user can clean up.

proceed.text: Use {equipment|the} for the job, following its instructions.
proceed.why: The equipment, gear and paperwork all check out, so the job can go ahead.
proceed.lesson: When the right equipment is ready and checked, use it as instructed.

generic.text: Ask {coworker2} to do the job instead, without telling {lead|the}.
generic.why: Passing the job on quietly confuses who is responsible for it.
generic.mis: Handing off a job avoids the problem.

generic.text: Adjust the settings to their highest level to finish faster.
generic.why: Running above normal settings can damage the work or the equipment.
generic.mis: Higher settings always mean faster, better work.

overcaution.text: Wait for {lead|the} to watch you use {equipment|the} the first time today.
overcaution.why: You know the model and are prepared. Waiting for supervision wastes time.

setup: You are {role|a} at {workplace|a}, about to use {equipment|the} for a job.

model: The {equipment} here is a model you have not used before.
signout: Equipment use must be signed for in {record|the}.

steps.text: Sign for it in the log
Review the instructions for this model

rel: The instructions tell you what to check on this model.
The instructions list the gear you need.
Damage has to be found before use.
Gear goes on before you start.
The rule says to sign before using it.
process.lesson: Sign out, learn the model, inspect, gear up, then do the job.

review.notes: Sign-out rule stated as posted policy; gear requirement attributed to the equipment instructions.

kits.familyName: Choosing the right tool for the task
setup: You are {role|a} at {workplace|a}, working on a task for {lead|the}.
detail: The task needs to be done by the end of the day.

fact: You need to total 200 numbers from {record|the}, and you were about to add them by hand.
issues.action: Put the numbers in a spreadsheet and let it calculate the total.
issues.reason: A spreadsheet is faster and far less error-prone than adding hundreds of numbers by hand.
issues.lesson: Choose tools that make the task faster and more accurate.

shortcut.text: Add them by hand twice to make sure the total is right.
shortcut.why: Doing it twice by hand doubles the time and still risks errors.
shortcut.mis: Doing it by hand is more reliable.

fact: The job needs an exact measurement, and you were going to estimate it by eye.
issues.action: Use a proper measuring tool so the measurement is exact.
issues.reason: An estimate can be off enough to ruin the work. A measuring tool gives the exact number.
issues.lesson: Use measuring tools when a job needs exact numbers.

shortcut.text: Estimate carefully, since you have a good eye.
shortcut.why: Even a good eye is not exact. The job needs a real measurement.

fact: You need to find a meeting time for ten people, and you planned to message each one separately.
issues.short: scheduling ten people one message at a time
issues.action: Use the shared calendar to find a time that works for everyone.
issues.reason: The shared calendar shows everyone's availability at once and saves dozens of messages.
issues.lesson: Use shared tools for tasks that involve many people.

shortcut.text: Pick a time yourself and hope most people can come.
shortcut.why: Guessing a time may leave people out when the calendar could show what works.
shortcut.mis: Picking a time is faster than checking.

fact: You need to make {document|a}, and the shared folder already has an approved template for it.
issues.action: Start from the approved template in the shared folder.
issues.reason: The template has the approved layout and required parts, which saves time and avoids missing pieces.
issues.lesson: Use approved templates instead of starting from scratch.

shortcut.text: Design a new layout from scratch so it looks fresh.
shortcut.why: A new layout may miss required parts and takes longer.

fact: You need to enter 80 item codes, and {system|the} can read them with a scanner.
issues.action: Use the scanner to enter the item codes.
issues.reason: Scanning is faster and avoids typing errors.
issues.lesson: Use the technology built for the task.

shortcut.text: Type each code by hand, since you type quickly.
shortcut.why: Typing 80 codes is slow and invites mistakes the scanner would avoid.
shortcut.mis: Fast typing beats the right tool.

fact: You need 50 matching labels, and you were about to write each one by hand.
issues.action: Use the label printer or a template to make all 50 labels.
issues.reason: A printer makes the labels faster, neater and identical.
issues.lesson: Use the tool built for repeated tasks.

shortcut.text: Write them by hand, since handwriting is more personal.
shortcut.why: Fifty handwritten labels take far longer and may be hard to read.
shortcut.mis: Doing it by hand is always better quality.

proceed.text: Do the task by hand the way you always have.
proceed.why: A better tool for this task is available, so the old way wastes time.
proceed.lesson: Picking the right tool is part of doing the job well.

generic.text: Ask {coworker} to do it, since they like that kind of task.
generic.why: Handing off the task avoids learning the tool you need.
generic.mis: Someone else's preference is a reason to hand off work.

generic.text: Skip the task and tell {lead|the} it was too slow to finish.
generic.why: The right tool makes the task manageable. Skipping it leaves the work undone.

title: Tool tips for new staff
intro: You are checking these tool tips before they go into the new-staff packet.
doc.lesson: Good tool guidance matches each task with the right, safe tool.

lines.text: Use the spreadsheet for totals and calculations.
lines.fine: Matches the task to the right tool.

bad.text: Add long lists of numbers by hand to avoid computer mistakes.
bad.why: Adding by hand is slower and more error-prone than a spreadsheet.

lines.text: Measure with the proper tool; do not estimate by eye.

bad.text: Estimate measurements by eye; it is faster.
bad.why: Estimates can be off enough to ruin the job; measure instead.

lines.text: Start documents from the approved templates.

bad.text: Start every document from a blank page.
bad.why: Approved templates contain required parts and save time.

lines.text: If a tool is busy, wait or ask {lead|the} about an approved alternative.

bad.text: If a tool is busy, use whatever is nearby that looks similar.
bad.why: Similar-looking tools may not be safe or accurate for the job.

lines.text: Read the instructions before using a model you do not know.

bad.text: All models work the same, so you can skip the instructions.
bad.why: Models differ in controls and limits; instructions should be read.

lines.text: Report damaged tools and tag them out of service.
lines.fine: Keeps damaged tools out of use.

bad.text: Tape over cracks on tools so they can keep being used.
bad.why: Taping a crack hides damage. The tool should be tagged out and reported.

review.notes: Tool-selection situations are beginner-only single decisions.
